content:
I know fairly well what I want to prove, and AI has been a massive help in actually generating the Lean proofs. I also heavily influence how I want the mathematics and the overall development to be framed. What I’m still lacking is experience with Lean and, in particular, with how developments should be structured for Physlib. As one can see in this PR #1510, this can lead to rather substantial changes during review.

At the moment I have a development of roughly 6k lines that characterizes quite a lot about the harmonic oscillator, with a larger mathematical storyline and some final classification results as the goal.

I’m wondering what the best way of handling something like this is. I could split it into many small, self-contained PRs, which would presumably make review much easier. But then I’m worried that it becomes difficult to see the end goal and why some of the intermediate definitions and results are being introduced in the first place.

Alternatively, is PhyslibAlpha intended for exactly this kind of situation? I could put the whole development there first, so that the complete code and mathematical storyline are visible to everyone, and then gradually extract/refactor pieces into proper Physlib PRs as they mature.

What workflow would you recommend for a development of this size?

Alternatively, is PhyslibAlpha intended for exactly this kind of situation?

Yes! This is exactly what this is for :).

But also don't be disheartened by the scale of changes asked. Getting things to fit within the library in the best way possible is a difficult task (and one for example AI certainly has not certainly not mastered IMO), but also one that hopefully leads to a much easier future for us all as we collectively expand the library. It's unfortunately only something that comes really through experience though, which makes it hard when one is setting out. One saying that goes around is that once you open the PR that is only half the work.

But a good workflow would be:

  • Put the stuff in PhyslibAlpha, so everyone can see/use it that wants to.
  • Move things slowly from PhyslibAlpha to Physlib with small PRs easy to review PRs.
